The Federal Fire Service Gombe State Command has commenced the 2026 National Fire Safety Awareness Week with a call to residents to embrace collective responsibility in preventing fire outbreaks. The awareness campaign, which began at the Multi-Purpose Hall of the Gombe State College of Nursing and Midwifery, featured a technical lecture and a multi-stakeholder panel discussion. Arewa PUNCH reports that the programme was organised under the theme: “Building a Resilient Nigeria: One Community at a Time.” Speaking at the event, the State Controller of the Federal Fire Service, Gombe Command, DCF Suleiman Suleiman, stressed the need for proactive measures, public education and community participation to reduce fire incidents. Suleiman said building a fire-resilient society required the collective efforts of individuals, institutions, government agencies and other relevant stakeholders. It also highlighted the need for households, workplaces and public facilities to adopt safety measures to minimise the risk of fire outbreaks. The discussions focused on improving emergency preparedness, strengthening public awareness and encouraging community participation in fire prevention. The command further noted that the awareness campaign would continue throughout the week with sensitisation visits to markets, schools and the Dankwambo Mega Motor Park. It added that the activities would culminate in a mega rally and roadshow across Gombe metropolis. The Federal Fire Service urged residents to identify potential fire hazards, handle electrical and cooking appliances safely and ensure that appropriate fire safety measures were installed in their homes and workplaces.
